newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle sees 1997 sales, profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Nestle sees 1997 sales, profit growth.

text.p: Nestle SA expects sales volume growth to accelerate in 1997 and both sales and profit to grow, Chairman and Chief Executive Helmut Maucher said in the company's annual report.

"For this year, we expect an acceleration in the growth of sales volumes and good progress in both sales and profits," he said in a letter to shareholders. "This development will be even more pronounced if the present currency levels are maintained."

Maucher said Nestle's optimism reflected its geographic and product diversification since the early 1980s, increased spending on research and development, the strengthening of its image and brands, management improvements and cost controls.

"While we remain open to the possibility of seizing strategic opportunities if they arise, acquisitions will play a lesser role in the group's development, which will be driven mainly by internal growth," he said.

Nestle sales grew 7.1 percent in 1996 to 60.49 billion Swiss francs ($41.1 billion). Sales volume growth remained below expectations at 2.7 percent, while currency exchange rates had a modest positive impact for the first time since 1993.
Operating margins stayed at 9.7 percent and net profit rose 16.6 percent to 3.40 billion, or 5.6 percent of sales compared with 5.2 percent the previous year.

In Europe, 1996 sales volume grew faster than expected, thanks in particular to strong development in Germany and eastern Europe, it said. Sales in central and eastern Europe had nearly doubled over the past two years.

"As a result of the acquisitons policy implemented since the early 1990s, the group now possesses a local base for a large variety of products. At the same time imports, especially of soluble coffees into Russia, have become very significant."
Citing its balanced portfolio of products, Nestle said it had diversified its risks and had laid a solid foundation for future growth, especially in emerging markets.

Acquisitions have given Nestle a strong position in ice cream and mineral water and rounded out activities in such lines as pet food, sectors that offer strong growth potential in both industrialised and emerging countries, it said.
It said new bottling centres would be inaugurated in China and Romania during 1997. The group also plans to extend its pet food activities in eastern Europe and other emerging markets.

Nestle noted that emerging markets accounted for 28 percent of sales in 1996, up from 26 percent in 1995. New markets such as those in eastern Europe account for part of the rise, as does its long-term presence in Latin America and Asia.
Nestle has also been actively reinforcing its presence in the Middle East, it said.
